opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. The two team notes conflict on the key fact: the HR note reports full_time employment (max write, since Analyst does not own Payroll), while the Security note reports contractor employment with basic security training (max read; contractors never get admin). Requested admin exceeds the maximum under either reading. Because the facts are conflicting and I cannot confirm the employee is entitled to the higher cap, I grant the most restrictive level that is policy-compliant under both interpretations, which is read.
